title: Small framed lifting tests for local fibrant objects
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and the model-category and homotopy-function-complex terminology of [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping] and the combinatorial and locally presentable terminology of [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a combinatorial model category with functorial factorizations, and let $S$ be a small set of arrows. Combinatorial means that the underlying category is locally presentable (cocomplete and generated under sufficiently filtered colimits by a small set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve these colimits) and each of its two weak factorization systems is generated by a small set of arrows under diagonal lifting. For an originally fibrant object $Z$, call $Z$ $S$-local if $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $(A\to B)\in S$. There exists a small set $H$ of original cofibrations such that an object $Z$ is originally fibrant and $S$-local if and only if its terminal map $Z\to1$ has the right lifting property against every member of $H$. Here the right lifting property means existence of a diagonal filler in every commuting square with that member on the left. Moreover, if $i:U\to V$ has cofibrant source and belongs to the weakly saturated class generated by $H$, then $\operatorname{Map}^h(V,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(U,Z)$ is an equivalence for every originally fibrant $S$-local $Z$. The weakly saturated class is the smallest class containing $H$ and all isomorphisms and closed under pushouts, small transfinite compositions continuous at limit stages, and retracts in the ordinary arrow category. No left properness or simplicial enrichment is assumed, and the endpoints of members of $S$ need not be cofibrant.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Definition 3.3.8, Proposition 3.3.9, Lemma 3.3.11, Theorem 17.8.4, Propositions 17.8.7-17.8.8, Corollary 17.8.12(1), Proposition 17.8.14(1), and the continuous-tower argument in the proof of Theorem 17.8.18 (printed pp. 60-61, 369-375). Core cellular formulation expanded by agent; Corollary 17.8.12(1) applies because horn endpoints and the current pushout object are cofibrant; original generating trivial cofibrations remain trivial under arbitrary pushout. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: Choose a small generating set $J$ for the weak factorization system $(C\cap W,F)$, not $(C,F\cap W)$. By the definition of a generated weak factorization system, $J^{\square}=F$ and every $j\in J$ is in ${}^{\square}F=C\cap W$. Consequently $Z\to1$ lifts against $J$ exactly when $Z$ is originally fibrant. No cofibrancy of the domains of $J$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Definitions of generated weak factorization systems and fibrant objects; Hirschhorn Definition 11.1.2. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: For each $s:A\to B$ in $S$, use [lem-cbc-framed-horn-criterion] to choose a Reedy-cofibration cosimplicial resolution of the arrow and its maps $h_{s,n}$ for every $n\geq0$. Set $H=J\cup\{h_{s,n}\mid s\in S,\ n\geq0\}$. The cited node states that every $h_{s,n}$ is an original cofibration with cofibrant endpoints; the maps in $J$ are original trivial cofibrations by step 1, without an endpoint-cofibrancy assertion. The union is small because it is indexed by the small sets $J$ and $S\times\mathbf N$. Thus $H$ is a small set of original cofibrations.

source.place: Definition 3.3.8(1), Proposition 3.3.9(1), Proposition 16.1.22(1) and Corollary 16.3.11(1). Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: If $Z$ is originally fibrant and $S$-local, step 1 gives lifting against $J$, and the boundary lifting equivalence in [lem-cbc-framed-horn-criterion] gives lifting against every $h_{s,n}$. Conversely, lifting against $H$ gives original fibrancy by step 1; the same criterion then says that each $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)$ is an equivalence. This proves the stated characterization of local fibrant objects.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.11(1) and Proposition 17.8.8(2)-(3). Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: Fix an originally fibrant $S$-local $Z$. Choose its simplicial resolution and the family $P_Z=\{p_n:Z_n\to M_nZ_\bullet\mid n\geq0\}$ supplied by [lem-cbc-right-resolution-mapping-criterion]. Every $p_n$ is an original fibration. Hence each $j\in J\subseteq C\cap W={}^{\square}F$ lifts against every $p_n$, including when the endpoints of $j$ are not cofibrant. For each $h_{s,n}$, the final mapping-equivalence assertion of [lem-cbc-framed-horn-criterion] applies because $s\in S$ and $Z$ is $S$-local, so $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)$ is an equivalence; its endpoints are cofibrant, so the right-resolution criterion makes $h_{s,n}$ lift against every $p_m$. Therefore $H\subseteq{}^{\square}P_Z$.

source.place: Theorem 17.8.4(4)-(5), Proposition 17.8.8(4)-(5), Proposition 17.8.14(1), and the weak factorization system $(C\cap W,F)$. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: Let $K$ be the weakly saturated class generated by $H$. For any class $T$, [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] gives closure of ${}^{\square}T$ under identities, pushouts and arrow retracts, and [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting] gives closure under small transfinite compositions continuous at limit stages. If an isomorphism $a:A\to B$ is the left side of a square with top map $u:A\to X$ and right side $p:X\to Y$, then $u a^{-1}:B\to X$ is its diagonal: $(u a^{-1})a=u$ and $p u a^{-1}=v a a^{-1}=v$. Hence ${}^{\square}T$ contains every isomorphism. With $T=P_Z$, step 4 and the defining minimality of $K$ give $K\subseteq{}^{\square}P_Z$. With $T=F\cap W$, the model-category lifting characterization is $C={}^{\square}(F\cap W)$. Since $H\subseteq C$ by steps 1 and 2, the displayed closure properties and minimality give $K\subseteq C$. Now let $i:U\to V$ belong to $K$ with $U$ cofibrant. Then $i$ is an original cofibration and lifts against every $p_n$. Applying [lem-cbc-right-resolution-mapping-criterion] gives that $\operatorname{Map}^h(V,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(U,Z)$ is an equivalence. This argument applies to each originally fibrant $S$-local $Z$ fixed in step 4.

source.place: Proposition 17.8.8(4)-(5), with ordinary left lifting closure under pushouts, transfinite compositions, and retracts (Hirschhorn Lemmas 7.2.11, 7.2.8 and Proposition 10.3.4). Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

split_report.summary: Continued the saved sandbox and retained the exact authoritative item statement. Corrected J to generate (trivial cofibrations, fibrations) and corrected Hirschhorn horns to boundary pushout corners including n=0. Five steps explicitly build H, prove the local fibrant characterization, and prove weak saturation by ordinary left lifting closure; no properness or simplicial enrichment is added.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q100-397316c1b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes and every cited node statement (frame-mapping, combinatorial-presentability, Reedy model structure, Kan-Quillen, both Mathlib-leaf lifting-closure nodes) in full; review.md has the full details. Hirschhorn is not archived and network access is blocked, so I checked the cited places (16.1.22, 16.3.x, 16.5.4, 16.6.9, 17.8.4/8/14) against what I know of the book and proved every assertion myself; the WANTED archive request stands. Step 1: J correctly generates (C∩W,F), so J^□=F and J⊆C∩W; marking it elementary is right. Step 2: H is small and consists of cofibrations. Step 3: both directions apply child 1 only after fibrancy is known. Step 4: each p_n is a fibration, so J lifts against it; for h_{s,n}, child 1's last clause plus cofibrant endpoints let child 2 (i)⇒(iii) apply. Step 5: the cited closure leaves give K⊆^□P_Z and K⊆C, and child 2 (iii)⇒(i) needs only cofibrant source. Horn criterion: resolutions of arbitrary arrows exist by factoring in the Reedy structure; h_{s,n} is a cofibration between cofibrant objects; h_{s,0}=s^0; the lifting statements follow from the coend adjunction; the last clause holds because X⊗K presents |K|⊗X, so the corner map of mapping spaces is an equivalence. Right-resolution criterion: Z_0=Z can be kept since Z→1 is a fibration; (ii)⇔(iii) follows from Hom(V,M_nZ)=sSet(∂Δ^n,R(V,Z_•)). Small cases: s=∅→pt with Z two points (correctly rejected, which confirms the horn-to-boundary repair), Z=∅, S empty, s an identity, Z terminal, u=∅→pt. No duplicate in a scan of all of dag/nodes; neither child restates the item and there is no cycle. I accept both declared tool_uses (definitional use only). No SGA is cited. lean.statement: theorem framed_localizing_cofibrations {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasLimits C] [HasColimits C] [ModelCategory C] (_hC : CombinatorialModelCategory.{u, v, w} C) (K : SSet.{max u v t}) (q : FiniteReedy.largeNerve.{u, v, t} C ⟶ K) (_hq : FiniteReedy.IsLocalization (weakEquivalences C) q) {I : Type w} (S : I → Arrow C) : ∃ (J : Type w) (H : J → Arrow C), (∀ j : J, Cofibration (H j).hom) ∧ (∀ Z : C, IsFramedLocal q S Z ↔ ∀ j : J, HasLiftingProperty (H j).hom (terminal.from Z)) ∧ ∀ (U V : C) (i : U ⟶ V), IsCofibrant U → (∀ W : MorphismProperty C, (∀ j : J, W (H j).hom) → MorphismProperty.isomorphisms C ≤ W → W.IsStableUnderCobaseChange → W.IsStableUnderTransfiniteComposition.{w} → W.IsStableUnderRetracts → W i) → ∀ Z : C, IsFramedLocal q S Z → framedMappingEquivalences q Z i
lean.note: Uses the recorded combinatorial structure and FrameMappingRelation to specify equivalence of canonical derived precomposition, without enrichment or endpoint cofibrancy assumptions on S. The two definition helpers render the locality terminology explicitly introduced in this node. Weak saturation uses its universal minimality property with Mathlib ordinary closure predicates. Small generators, S, H and transfinite compositions share an arbitrary universe w, independently of object and morphism universes.
